The master manuscript now rules out a **smooth complete time-zero limit** in the modified Ricci concentration branch, under one additional geometric hypothesis. In a fixed strictly subcritical band, assume the spectral deficit tends to zero and the modified metrics satisfy \(\operatorname{Vol}B(x,r)\le Vr^4\) through a common positive radius. Then an actual shrinking ball carries definite trace-free Ricci energy. At the first such curvature scale, smoothing yields a complete, noncompact, nonflat positive-time flow with nonnegative isotropic curvature. The decisive step is that a **nonzero negative Euler measure survives as time tends to zero**. The original Yamabe inequality also survives on compact tests. Together they exclude even subsequential locally uniform, strong \(W^{1,4}\) convergence to a smooth complete metric in the fixed flow markings. Establishing the upper volume bound on the actual modified sequence, or understanding its failure, remains open. [Master manuscript, 35 pages](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/output/pdf/master/chiral_weyl_energy_and_smooth_poincare.pdf)

On the original E61 disk, the normalized Bach pairing and the negative part of the second variation are both \(O(\sqrt{e_i-I})\), with cutoffs measured at their actual widths. A positive variation confined to the disk can save at most \(e_i-I\). Thus a matched enlarged-disk repair must transfer its required saving into the exterior, including the protected-core contribution. **No strict same-type repair was obtained.** [Fixed-type descent manuscript](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/output/pdf/master/01_fixed_type_variational_descent/fixed_type_chiral_energy_descent.pdf)

The parallel branches reduced the prescribed eta-zero filling to a Robin trace test on an actual extension, derived proper flat embeddings under buffered physical curvature control, and located both gauges’ full curvature on one exit under smooth round comparison. No additional smooth type was recognized.
